# Equal-budget caps retain curved rigidity under a fixed box constraint

This is a restricted obstruction, not an unrestricted polytope-replacement
counterexample. It identifies exactly what the equal-budget restriction does
and does not remove from the earlier four-dimensional example.

Use coordinates (x_1,x_2,t,s), let B be the unit disk, and set

    C=B times [0,3]^2,     |C|=9 pi,
    alpha=1/4, epsilon=1/10, a=sqrt(1799)/20.

Consider convex bodies L contained in

    R=[-2,2]^2 times [0,3]^2.                            (1)

Every one of the following fourteen halfspaces cuts exactly alpha |C| from C:

* t<=3/4, t>=9/4, s<=3/4, s>=9/4;
* for i=1,2, t<=3/4+epsilon x_i, t>=9/4+epsilon x_i,
  s<=3/4+epsilon x_i, s>=9/4+epsilon x_i;
* for i=1,2, t+s<=a+epsilon x_i.

All are proper positive caps. No zero-volume, full-volume, or nested pair of
same-oriented parallel cap constraints occurs. Together with total volume,
they uniquely determine C among convex bodies satisfying (1). In particular,
no polytope in that constrained class matches them.

## A concave-root profile rigidity lemma

Let f:[0,L]->[0,infinity) be integrable and not identically zero. Suppose
f^(1/r) is concave on its positive support, with convex support (r>0).
Write m=L^(-1) integral f. If, for 0<q<L/2,

    integral_0^q f=q m,
    integral_(L-q)^L f=q m,                              (2)

then f=m almost everywhere on [0,L]. The same statement holds for any
log-concave f.

Choose t_left in [0,q] and t_right in [L-q,L] with
f(t_left)>=m and f(t_right)>=m; such points exist from the two tail
averages (using approximate points and limits if necessary). Concavity of
the root, or of log f, implies f>=m throughout [q,L-q]. But its integral
on that middle interval is exactly m(L-2q), so f=m there. A concave
function constant on a nontrivial interval is no larger than that constant
outside that interval: compare its secant slopes with the zero slopes on
the constant interval. Thus f<=m on each outer interval within its support,
and also outside its support where f=0. Their average equalities force
f=m almost everywhere there as well. This proves the lemma.

## The four untilted caps force a double prism

Apply the lemma to the t-section volume of L with L=3 and q=3/4.
Its 1/3 power is concave on its actual projection by ordinary
Brunn--Minkowski; set the section volume to zero elsewhere in [0,3]. The prescribed total and two
quartile-tail volumes force the section volume to equal 3 pi throughout
[0,3]. Equal section volumes and equality in Brunn--Minkowski force all
sections to be translates, with an affine translation vector. Thus L is a
t-prism. Repeat in s.

To remove cross-shear, the (t,s)-projection of a t-prism is a parallelogram
with constant positive vertical section length. The s-prism structure gives
constant positive horizontal section length. A sheared parallelogram has
horizontal section lengths tending to zero at one extreme, so its shear
must vanish. The projection is [0,3]^2. Consequently

    L={(y+t v+s w,t,s): y in K, 0<=t,s<=3}               (3)

for a planar body K of area pi. The shear vectors v,w belong to R^2.

## The eight tilted caps remove all remaining shear

Write m for the centroid of K. Containment in (1) gives |v_i|,|w_i|<=4/3.
Every tilted threshold stays strictly between 0 and 3, because the original
cap margins at t=0 and t=3 have opposite signs for |x_i|<=2; similarly in s.
The top t-cap equation is

    m_i+(3/2)w_i=-(9/4)v_i.

The bottom t-cap equation is

    m_i+(3/2)w_i=-(3/4)v_i.

They follow by solving the cut for t, integrating the affine threshold over
K times [0,3], and using its prescribed fraction 1/4. Thus v_i=0 and
m_i+(3/2)w_i=0. The two s-equations give w_i=0 and m_i=0. Hence

    L=K times [0,3]^2,       centroid(K)=0.              (4)

## The two corner caps force the disk

Because K subset [-2,2]^2 and 0<a-1/5<a+1/5<3, their square sections have
areas (a+epsilon y_i)^2/2. Their prescribed volume 9 pi/4 therefore gives

    a^2 pi/2+(epsilon^2/2) integral_K y_i^2=9 pi/4.

Since a^2=9/2-epsilon^2/4,

    integral_K y_i^2=pi/4, i=1,2.

The unit disk uniquely minimizes integral |y|^2 among measurable planar
sets of area pi. Indeed the difference from its value equals

    integral_(K\B)(|y|^2-1)+integral_(B\K)(1-|y|^2)>=0,

with equality only up to a null set, hence exactly for convex bodies.
Thus K=B.

## Scope and a simpler four-cap subcertificate

The box restriction (1) is essential to the argument and is NOT supplied
by the fourteen equal-budget measurements. No conclusion is asserted for
an unrestricted candidate L. In the still narrower fixed product family
K times [0,3]^2, just the two top tilted caps and the two corner caps,
together with total volume, already force K=B.

This shows that equal budgets alone do not eliminate moment rigidity of a
curved factor when admissible variations preserve a product structure or a
fixed outer box. A proof of unrestricted replacement must exploit the
ability to move the outer facets or establish an additional low-depth
property that supplies such a motion.
